summary.text: Data engineer who builds and operates production data infrastructure end-to-end. Solo-built a 75 GB, 120M+ row market-data system with bitemporal point-in-time versioning, daily entity-state reconciliation across ~3,900 entities, self-healing backfills, and standing data-quality automation. Also ship a live AI platform that ingests 180K+ records from nine heterogeneous external sources with schema normalization, multi-tier caching, and CI-gated API contracts.

education.degree: B.S. Computational Data Science & Statistics (Double Major)

bullets.text: Engineered a Postgres-native async ingestion pipeline (Procrastinate cron) across major ATS platforms — **Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Workable, and Oracle Recruiting Cloud** — plus **LinkedIn and Indeed**, normalizing heterogeneous schemas into a shared index of **180K+ postings**.

Designed a **multi-tier cache** (normalized-URL → ATS API → metered LLM) with SHA-256 content-hash deduplication and cross-source identity merge, so duplicate records resolve on a **$0 path** instead of re-triggering paid extraction.

Built **record-lifecycle hygiene** over that index — active/expired classification, dead-link and garbage-record detection, and periodic revalidation — so downstream scoring runs against records that are still valid.

Built the backend on FastAPI · SQLModel · PostgreSQL 17 with a 25-table **row-level-security** schema and contract-first Pydantic → OpenAPI → TypeScript codegen **gated in CI**, eliminating client/schema drift.

Integrated Google and Microsoft **OAuth** with Gmail / Outlook and Calendar via **Cloud Pub/Sub push receivers and Microsoft Graph webhooks**, with a scope-isolated encrypted token store and automatic subscription renewal.
Self-host a fine-tuned LLM (Qwen 3.6 9B, QLoRA → **vLLM with NVFP4 quantization**) plus an embedding retrieval layer, with per-call cost metering and a CI gate on prompt changes.
Built a Python NLP pipeline that classified 150+ unstructured intelligence reports, cutting manual analysis time **60%**.
Developed an anomaly-detection system flagging high-priority events at **85% precision**.

Architected and operate a **75 GB PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB** system — **over 120M rows** across 89 tables and 18 hypertables — ingesting from **26 sources** (REST and SDMX APIs plus three anti-bot crawlers) on **18 systemd timers** with a dead-letter retry queue and a ~30-second intraday event daemon.

Implemented **bitemporal point-in-time versioning** (vintage-dated, UPSERT-only history) and an **amendment-supersession resolver over 135K record versions** that reconstructs each record's true original publication timestamp — closing a correctness defect in which later amendments masked when data actually became available.

Maintain a **daily-reconciled slowly-changing entity dimension**: ~2,800 active entities out of 3,900+ historical, with roughly **50 state transitions per day** across an eight-state status model, rebuilt daily rather than snapshotted — preserving full history including retired entities.

Operate **self-healing multi-day backfills** (file-lock + checkpoint + resumable) that reconstructed 342K rows spanning 2008–2023 with no manual intervention, plus daily automated health and coverage alerting.

Run **standing data-quality automation** — daily cross-table reconciliation, staleness detection, coverage-gap and dimension-diff audits — with an audit yielding **0 future-dated rows, 0 duplicate keys, and 0 time-series gaps** across core tables.
Built a read-only **schema-and-lineage explorer** rendering **97 table relationships**, column-level lineage, and eight-band freshness into a single self-contained HTML view.
Deployed **KR-FinBERT** GPU inference over **860K+ text rows** (BFloat16, torch.compile, CUDA-OOM-adaptive batching) and implemented **121 registered features across 3 layers**.

Built a conditional predictive-distribution pipeline over **30 years** of index data (1996–2026), implementing GARCH and particle-filter models from scratch and validating each by synthetic parameter recovery.
